set.hook: The Roca brothers' Girona flagship, three MICHELIN stars and forty years old in 2026.
set.why: Joan, Josep and Jordi Roca opened El Celler in 1986 beside their parents' family restaurant in Taialà, on the edge of Girona, and the house turns forty this year. To mark it, Joan Roca presented a menu of forty small dishes at San Sebastián Gastronomika on 5 October 2026, built around the tasting format and using augmented reality at the table. The standing menu, Festival, runs to snacks, twelve dishes and three desserts, and the whole table eats it.
set.verdict: The grand night of the coast, for guests who will plan a trip around one dinner. Book the Festival menu with Josep Roca's wine pairing, and ask whether the fortieth-anniversary menu is being served on your date.

set.hook: Albert Sastregener's two-star kitchen in an old carriage works on the road through Corçà.
set.why: Bo.TiC opened in 2007 and took its second MICHELIN star in the 2021 guide, announced in December 2020 alongside Cinc Sentits and Culler de Pau. Albert Sastregener had already held a star at La Cocina de Can Pipes in Mont-ras. The room is a former carriage factory: one dining room looks into the kitchen, the other sits inside old stone walls, and one local grower raises Japanese vegetables and shoots for the menus.
set.verdict: The quieter of the coast's two-star tables, for a long lunch inland from Palamós. Start with the Degustación menu; take the Del Chef menu only if the table wants the full afternoon.

set.hook: A roadside masia on the Sant Feliu road, run by the Gascons siblings, starred since 2008.
set.why: Els Tinars began in 1978 as a roadside restaurant that the Gascons parents opened in a centuries-old farmhouse beside the Costa Brava road; their own parents had run the Bahía in Sant Feliu de Guíxols in the 1950s. Marc Gascons now cooks and runs it with his sister Elena, and in July 2025 he won the Premi Nacional de Gastronomia for author cuisine. The most requested dish is a tartare of Palamós prawn whose garnish changes with the season.
set.verdict: For guests who want serious Catalan cooking without a laboratory feel, at a fraction of the two- and three-star bills. Order the Palamós prawn tartare and the seasonal menu.

set.hook: A family hotel kitchen on the steps above Llafranc bay, seventy years old in 2026.
set.why: Casamar is a family house that the Casellas siblings say turns seventy this year; their grandparents opened it. Quim Casellas won its first MICHELIN star in late 2011, for the 2012 guide, and lost it around 2021; he told Ara this January that losing it left the family feeling abandoned by the press. They spent the winter rebuilding the hotel upstairs, from twenty-one rooms to eighteen larger ones, and reopened the kitchen on 27 March 2026.
set.verdict: For a sunset dinner over the bay with cooking more careful than the cove usually offers. Order from the rice section, or take the Punta d'en Blanc menu if the table wants a set run.

set.hook: Peratallada's oldest dining room, under the arcades of Plaça de les Voltes, cooking goose with turnips.
set.why: The Bonay family opened this restaurant in 1936 in an old manor house on the arcaded square of Peratallada, and it has passed from father to son since; listings name the brothers Josep and Enric Bonay as today's managers. Its best-known plate is oca amb naps, goose braised with turnips, the Empordà winter dish, and the kitchen also cooks game in season. Reviewers call it the oldest restaurant in the village.
set.verdict: For a slow lunch on a day ashore in the medieval villages, not for a fine-dining night. Order the goose with turnips and the house wine.

set.hook: Shared plates from the three chefs behind Disfrutar, in an old stone house on the Cadaqués riverbed.
set.why: Before Disfrutar in Barcelona, Mateu Casañas, Oriol Castro and Eduard Xatruch, who met in the elBulli kitchen at Cala Montjoi over the hill, opened this room in Cadaqués in 2012. The rule is in the name: nothing arrives as an individual plate, everything goes to the middle. The chef's menu now runs to about ten savoury courses and three sweets. Their Barcelona house later took a third star (November 2023) and the World's 50 Best No.1 (June 2024).
set.verdict: For a long shared lunch with the whole table on one menu, and the closest the coast gets to the elBulli lineage at a fraction of the Barcelona bill. Go with an open mind on the menu and start with the gazpacho.

summit.title: Stars between Girona and Llagostera
summit.story: The starred cooking of this coast sits inland, a short drive from the berths at Palamós. In Girona, El Celler de Can Roca opened in 1986 beside the Roca parents' family restaurant in Taialà, holds three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide and marked forty years in October 2026 with a menu of forty small dishes. In Corçà, Albert Sastregener's Bo.TiC works in a former carriage factory and took its second star in the 2021 guide. On the road from Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Els Tinars began as a roadside masia in 1978; it has held a star since 2008, and the siblings Marc and Elena Gascons run it, Marc cooking a Palamós prawn tartare that changes with the season.
summit.where: El Celler de Can Roca, Girona; Bo.TiC, Corçà; Els Tinars, Llagostera

village.title: Cove, village and cape
village.story: Away from the starred line, the coast eats in family houses and small rooms that close or slow down in winter. Casamar, on the steps above Llafranc bay, marks seventy years in 2026; Quim Casellas held a MICHELIN star there from the 2012 guide until about 2021, and the kitchen reopened on 27 March after the hotel was rebuilt. Inland at Peratallada, the Bonay family has served goose braised with turnips under the arcades of Plaça de les Voltes since 1936. At the cape end, in Cadaqués, the three chefs who later made Disfrutar opened Compartir in 2012, where every plate goes to the middle of the table.
village.where: Casamar, Llafranc; Can Bonay, Peratallada; Compartir, Cadaqués
